10:+/-!
11:+# The operator-valued BLR bound
13:+This file carries out the Fourier-analytic part of the proof of the quantum
14:+linearity theorem of Natarajan and Vidick.  Given binary observables `O^u`
15:+indexed by the Boolean cube `(ZMod 2)^t` and a positive semidefinite trace-one
16:+operator `ρ`, it expresses the state-dependent multiplicative defect of the
17:+family through the two-query correlation of the linearity test, identifies the
18:+sum of the cubic Fourier coefficients with that correlation, and records the
19:+overlap certificate for the Fourier-square POVM `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` that the
20:+Naimark dilation consumes.  Pairwise commutation of the observables is never
21:+assumed, and every complex trace is handled through its real part.
23:+## Main results
25:+* `multiplicativeDefect`: the state-dependent squared defect of `O^u O^v`
26:+  from `O^{u+v}`.
27:+* `avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation` and
28:+  `avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error`: the average defect equals
29:+  `2 - 2 * (correlation)`, hence is at most `2 * δ` under the correlation
30:+  hypothesis of `exists_exactly_linear_observables`.
31:+* `operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation`: the identity
32:+  `∑_u Tr_ρ((hat O^u)^3) = E_{a,b} Tr_ρ(O^a O^b O^{a+b})`.
33:+* `fourierSquareMeasurement` and `one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare`:
34:+  the Fourier-square POVM together with its overlap certificate.
36:+## References
38:+Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574, Theorem 10 with displays (7)--(8) and
39:+its proof, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1113`; the state-dependent
40:+distance is defined at lines 866--900 of the same file.  The QPBT paper quotes
41:+the theorem at
42:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725` and
43:+invokes it at lines 787--832.  The blueprint statement is `thm:linearity` in
44:+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:81-147`.  The normalization of
45:+the error constant is analyzed in
46:+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`: the exact defect
47:+bound is `2 * δ` for the raw distance `stateDepDistSq`, equivalently `δ` for
48:+the normalized binary-observable distance.
49:+-/
51:+open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
53:+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
55:+open MIPStarRE.LDT
56:+open MIPStarRE.Quantum
58:+noncomputable section
60:+/-! ## The two-query correlation and the multiplicative defect -/
62:+/-- The two-query correlation of the linearity test: the average, over a
63:+uniformly random pair `(u, u')` in `(ZMod 2)^t`, of the real part of
64:+`Tr(O^u O^{u'} O^{u+u'} ρ)`.  This is the left-hand side of display (7) in
65:+Natarajan--Vidick, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`, and the
66:+quantity bounded below in the hypothesis of
67:+`exists_exactly_linear_observables`; the order of the two uniform variables is
68:+the one used there. -/
69:+def blrCorrelation {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
70:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
71:+  avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
72:+    (fun pair =>
73:+      (Matrix.trace (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)
75:+/-- The state-dependent squared defect of the product `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}`,
76:+namely `d_ρ(O^u O^v, O^{u+v})^2` for the state-dependent distance of
77:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:873-875`.  Its average over uniformly random
78:+`u, v` is the approximate-linearity error of the family in the sense of the QPBT
79:+quotation `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`,
80:+measured with the raw distance `stateDepDistSq`. -/
81:+def multiplicativeDefect {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
82:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℝ :=
83:+  stateDepDistSq (O u * O v) (O (u + v)) ρ
85:+/-- Pointwise form of the defect identity: for binary observables the squared
86:+defect of `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}` is `2 - 2 Re Tr(O^v O^u O^{v+u} ρ)`.  The
87:+expansion of `(O^u O^v - O^{u+v})^† (O^u O^v - O^{u+v})` produces the two
88:+triple products `O^v O^u O^{u+v}` and `O^{u+v} O^u O^v`; the second is the
89:+adjoint of the first, so their traces against `ρ` are complex conjugates with
90:+equal real parts.  This is the calculation behind display (3) of
91:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912`, applied to the products of the
92:+family. -/
93:+theorem multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
94:+    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
95:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
96:+    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
97:+    (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
98:+    multiplicativeDefect O ρ u v =
99:+      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (v + u) * ρ)).re := by
100:+  have hu := hO u
101:+  have hv := hO v
102:+  have huv := hO (u + v)
103:+  have hdiff :
104:+      (O u * O v - O (u + v))ᴴ * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
105:+        (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) - O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
106:+    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq,
107:+      huv.1.eq]
108:+    calc
109:+      (O v * O u - O (u + v)) * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
110:+          O v * (O u * O u) * O v - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
111:+            O (u + v) * O u * O v + O (u + v) * O (u + v) := by
112:+        noncomm_ring
113:+      _ = (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
114:+            O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
115:+        rw [hu.2, Matrix.mul_one, hv.2, huv.2]
116:+        module
117:+  have hstar :
118:+      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
119:+        Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
120:+    calc
121:+      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
122:+          Matrix.trace ((O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)ᴴ) := by
123:+        rw [Matrix.trace_conjTranspose]
124:+      _ = Matrix.trace (ρ * (O v * O u * O (u + v))) := by
125:+        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq, huv.1.eq,
126:+          hρ.isHermitian.eq, Matrix.mul_assoc]
127:+      _ = Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
128:+        exact Matrix.trace_mul_comm _ _
129:+  have hcross :
130:+      (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)).re =
131:+        (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ)).re := by
132:+    have := congrArg Complex.re hstar
133:+    simpa [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] using this
134:+  unfold multiplicativeDefect stateDepDistSq
135:+  rw [hdiff]
136:+  simp only [Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.trace_sub, Complex.sub_re]
137:+  rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul, Matrix.trace_smul, htrace]
138:+  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
139:+  rw [hcross, add_comm v u]
140:+  ring
142:+/-- The average multiplicative defect over a uniformly random pair equals
143:+`2 - 2 * (two-query correlation)`.  The pointwise identity
144:+`multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation` produces the correlation
145:+summand with the two variables in reversed order; since the pair is uniform,
146:+exchanging the two coordinates leaves the average unchanged.  This is the
147:+relation between the approximate-linearity hypothesis of the QPBT quotation
148:+(`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`) and
149:+display (7) of Natarajan--Vidick (`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`),
150:+in the raw normalization of
151:+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
152:+theorem avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
153:+    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
154:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
155:+    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1) :
156:+    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
157:+        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) =
158:+      2 - 2 * blrCorrelation O ρ := by
159:+  have hswap :
160:+      avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
161:+        (fun pair =>
162:+          (Matrix.trace (O pair.2 * O pair.1 * O (pair.2 + pair.1) * ρ)).re) =
163:+        blrCorrelation O ρ := by
164:+    unfold blrCorrelation
165:+    refine (avgOver_uniform_equiv (Equiv.prodComm _ _) _).trans ?_
166:+    exact avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun pair => rfl)
167:+  calc
168:+    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
169:+        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) =
170:+        avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
171:+          (fun pair => 2 - 2 *
172:+            (Matrix.trace (O pair.2 * O pair.1 * O (pair.2 + pair.1) * ρ)).re) :=
173:+      avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun pair =>
174:+        multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation O hO ρ hρ htrace
175:+          pair.1 pair.2)
176:+    _ = 2 - 2 * blrCorrelation O ρ := by
177:+      rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_mul, avgOver_uniform_const, hswap]
179:+/-- The operator-valued BLR bound: under the correlation hypothesis of
180:+`exists_exactly_linear_observables`, the average squared defect of `O^u O^v`
181:+from `O^{u+v}` is at most `2 * δ`.  This is the passage from display (7) of
182:+Natarajan--Vidick (`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`) to the
183:+approximate-linearity relation of the QPBT quotation
184:+(`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`); the
185:+constant `2` is the raw-distance normalization recorded in
186:+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
187:+theorem avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error {t : ℕ}
188:+    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
189:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
190:+    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
191:+    (δ : ℝ) (hcorrelation : 1 - δ ≤ blrCorrelation O ρ) :
192:+    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
193:+        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) ≤ 2 * δ := by
194:+  rw [avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation O hO ρ hρ htrace]
195:+  linarith
197:+/-! ## The cubic Fourier identity -/
199:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier computations in the
200:+proof of Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick
201:+(`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1096-1112`): a twisted form of the
202:+matrix-valued Parseval identity in which only the first factor is expanded
203:+through its Fourier coefficients.  Taking `a = 0` recovers Parseval. -/
204:+private theorem sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul {t : ℕ}
205:+    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
206:+    (A X : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
207:+    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
208:+        booleanCharacter u a • (operatorFourier A u * X u) =
209:+      ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
210:+        ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
211:+          A b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u (a + b) • X u := by
212:+  classical
213:+  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
214:+  calc
215:+    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
216:+        booleanCharacter u a • (operatorFourier A u * X u) =
217:+        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
218:+          booleanCharacter u (a + b) • (A b * X u) := by
219:+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
220:+      intro u _
221:+      simp only [operatorFourier, N, smul_mul_assoc, Finset.sum_mul,
222:+        Finset.smul_sum, smul_smul, booleanCharacter_add_right]
223:+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
224:+      intro b _
225:+      congr 1
226:+      ring
227:+    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
228:+          booleanCharacter u (a + b) • (A b * X u) := by
229:+      rw [← Finset.smul_sum]
230:+      congr 1
231:+      exact Finset.sum_comm
232:+    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
233:+          A b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u (a + b) • X u := by
234:+      congr 1
235:+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
236:+      intro b _
237:+      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
238:+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
239:+      intro u _
240:+      rw [mul_smul_comm]
242:+/-- The sum of the cubes of the Fourier coefficients of an operator family is
243:+the average of `O^a O^b O^{a+b}` over a uniformly random pair `(a, b)`.  This
244:+is the operator form of the identity
245:+`∑_u (hat A^u)^3 = E_{a,b} A(a) A(b) A(a+b)` invoked at
246:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1111-1112`; the order of the three factors
247:+is preserved throughout. -/
248:+theorem sum_operatorFourier_cube {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
249:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) :
250:+    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
251:+        operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u =
252:+      ((Fintype.card ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
253:+        ∑ p : (Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2),
254:+          O p.1 * O p.2 * O (p.1 + p.2) := by
255:+  classical
256:+  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
257:+  have hinner : ∀ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
258:+      ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
259:+          booleanCharacter u b • (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) =
260:+        N⁻¹ • ∑ c : Fin t → ZMod 2, O c * O (b + c) := by
261:+    intro b
262:+    rw [sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul]
263:+    congr 1
264:+    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
265:+    intro c _
266:+    rw [operatorFourier_inversion]
267:+  calc
268:+    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
269:+        operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u =
270:+        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u 0 •
271:+          (operatorFourier O u * (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) := by
272:+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
273:+      intro u _
274:+      rw [booleanCharacter_zero_right, one_smul, Matrix.mul_assoc]
275:+    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, O b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
276:+          booleanCharacter u (0 + b) •
277:+            (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) := by
278:+      rw [sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul]
279:+    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
280:+          O b * (N⁻¹ • ∑ c : Fin t → ZMod 2, O c * O (b + c)) := by
281:+      simp only [zero_add, hinner]
282:+    _ = (N⁻¹ * N⁻¹) • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ c : Fin t → ZMod 2,
283:+          O b * O c * O (b + c) := by
284:+      simp only [mul_smul_comm, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.smul_sum, smul_smul,
285:+        Matrix.mul_assoc]
286:+    _ = ((Fintype.card ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
287:+          ∑ p : (Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2),
288:+            O p.1 * O p.2 * O (p.1 + p.2) := by
289:+      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type, Fintype.card_prod, Nat.cast_mul, mul_inv]
291:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the averages in this file: a uniform
292:+average over a nonempty finite type is the sum divided by the cardinality. -/
293:+private theorem avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum {α : Type*}
294:+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] (f : α → ℝ) :
295:+    avgOver (uniformDistribution α) f = (Fintype.card α : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ a, f a := by
296:+  simp [avgOver, uniformDistribution, Distribution.uniformOnFinset_weight,
297:+    Finset.mul_sum]
299:+/-- The sum of the cubic Fourier coefficients evaluated in `ρ` equals the
300:+two-query correlation:
301:+`∑_u Re Tr((hat O^u)^3 ρ) = E_{a,b} Re Tr(O^a O^b O^{a+b} ρ)`.  This is the
302:+identity stated at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1111-1112`, with the
303:+complex traces compared through their real parts. -/
304:+theorem operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation {t : ℕ}
305:+    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
306:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) :
307:+    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
308:+        (Matrix.trace (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u *
309:+          operatorFourier O u * ρ)).re =
310:+      blrCorrelation O ρ := by
311:+  rw [← Complex.re_sum, ← Matrix.trace_sum, ← Finset.sum_mul,
312:+    sum_operatorFourier_cube, smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul, Finset.sum_mul,
313:+    Matrix.trace_sum]
314:+  unfold blrCorrelation
315:+  rw [avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum, smul_eq_mul, ← Complex.ofReal_natCast,
316:+    ← Complex.ofReal_inv, Complex.re_ofReal_mul, Complex.re_sum]
318:+/-! ## The Fourier-square POVM and its overlap certificate -/
320:+/-- Each Fourier square `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` of a Hermitian operator family is
321:+positive semidefinite, being the product of a Hermitian matrix with its
322:+adjoint.  This is the positivity half of the assertion that the `B^u` form a
323:+POVM at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1098-1099`. -/
324:+theorem operatorFourier_mul_self_posSemidef {t : ℕ}
325:+    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
326:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, (O a).IsHermitian)
327:+    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
328:+    (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u).PosSemidef := by
329:+  have h := operatorFourier_isHermitian O hO u
330:+  simpa [h.eq] using
331:+    Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self (operatorFourier O u)
333:+/-- The Fourier-square POVM `{B^u = (hat O^u)^2}` of a family of binary
334:+observables, with outcomes in `(ZMod 2)^t`.  Positivity is
335:+`operatorFourier_mul_self_posSemidef` and completeness is the Parseval
336:+identity `sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one`.  This is the POVM to which Naimark's
337:+theorem is applied at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1097-1100`. -/
338:+def fourierSquareMeasurement {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
339:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
340:+    Measurement (Fin t → ZMod 2) ι :=
341:+  Measurement.ofSumEqOne
342:+    (fun u => operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)
343:+    (fun u => (operatorFourier_mul_self_posSemidef O (fun a => (hO a).1) u).nonneg)
344:+    (sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one O hO)
346:+/-- The effects of the Fourier-square POVM are the squares of the Fourier
347:+coefficients. -/
348:+@[simp]
349:+theorem fourierSquareMeasurement_effect {t : ℕ}
350:+    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
351:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
352:+    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
353:+    (fourierSquareMeasurement O hO).effect u =
354:+      operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u :=
355:+  rfl
357:+/-- The average state-dependent overlap between `O^a` and the character sum
358:+`∑_u (-1)^{u·a} B^u` of the Fourier-square POVM equals the sum of the cubic
359:+Fourier coefficients evaluated in `ρ`.  This is the computation of
360:+`E_a Re Tr_{ρ'}(A(a) 𝒜(a))` at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1104-1110`,
361:+carried out before the Naimark dilation: the character sum is the compression
362:+of the exactly linear observable `𝒜(a) = ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} C^u` to the original
363:+space. -/
364:+theorem avg_overlap_fourierSquare_eq_sum_cube {t : ℕ}
365:+    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
366:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) :
367:+    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
368:+        (fun a => (Matrix.trace (O a *
369:+          (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a •
370:+            (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) * ρ)).re) =
371:+      ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
372:+        (Matrix.trace (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u *
373:+          operatorFourier O u * ρ)).re := by
374:+  classical
375:+  have hop :
376:+      ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
377:+          operatorFourier O u * (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) =
378:+        ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
379:+          ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, O b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
380:+            booleanCharacter u b • (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) := by
381:+    have := sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul O
382:+      (fun u => operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) 0
383:+    simpa only [booleanCharacter_zero_right, one_smul, zero_add] using this
384:+  symm
385:+  calc
386:+    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
387:+        (Matrix.trace (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u *
388:+          operatorFourier O u * ρ)).re =
389:+        (Matrix.trace ((∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
390:+          operatorFourier O u * (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) *
391:+            ρ)).re := by
392:+      rw [Finset.sum_mul, Matrix.trace_sum, Complex.re_sum]
393:+      simp only [Matrix.mul_assoc]
394:+    _ = (Matrix.trace ((((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
395:+          ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, O b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
396:+            booleanCharacter u b • (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) *
397:+              ρ)).re := by
398:+      rw [hop]
399:+    _ = (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
400:+          ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, (Matrix.trace (O b *
401:+            (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u b •
402:+              (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) * ρ)).re := by
403:+      rw [smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul, Finset.sum_mul, Matrix.trace_sum,
404:+        smul_eq_mul, ← Complex.ofReal_natCast, ← Complex.ofReal_inv,
405:+        Complex.re_ofReal_mul, Complex.re_sum]
406:+    _ = avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
407:+          (fun a => (Matrix.trace (O a *
408:+            (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a •
409:+              (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) * ρ)).re) := by
410:+      rw [avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum]
412:+/-- The overlap certificate for the Fourier-square POVM: under the correlation
413:+hypothesis of `exists_exactly_linear_observables`, the average state-dependent
414:+overlap between `O^a` and the character sum `∑_u (-1)^{u·a} B^u` is at least
415:+`1 - δ`.  This is the conclusion of the computation at
416:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1104-1112` in the form consumed after the
417:+Naimark dilation: the same overlap, evaluated in `ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|` against the
418:+exactly linear observables, is what bounds the average distance in display (8).
419:+No commutation among the observables is used. -/
420:+theorem one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare {t : ℕ}
421:+    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
422:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι)
423:+    (δ : ℝ) (hcorrelation : 1 - δ ≤ blrCorrelation O ρ) :
424:+    1 - δ ≤ avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
425:+        (fun a => (Matrix.trace (O a *
426:+          (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a •
427:+            (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) * ρ)).re) := by
428:+  rw [avg_overlap_fourierSquare_eq_sum_cube,
429:+    operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation]
430:+  exact hcorrelation
432:+end

444:+/-!
445:+# Boolean Fourier analysis for the quantum linearity theorem
447:+This file develops the finite Fourier identities used in the proof of the
448:+quantum linearity theorem.  The Boolean characters are the additive characters
449:+of `𝔽_2^t`; their orthogonality gives Fourier inversion and matrix-valued
450:+Parseval for operator families.  The final section records the normalization
451:+relating the state-dependent operator distance to the distance between the
452:+associated binary projective measurements.
454:+## References
456:+The Fourier and Parseval argument is Theorem 10, equations (7)--(8), and its
457:+proof in `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1112`.  The observable-distance
458:+calculation is in the same source at lines 900--912.  The QPBT paper invokes
459:+this theorem in
460:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725`.
461:+-/
463:+open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
465:+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
467:+open MIPStarRE.LDT
468:+open MIPStarRE.Quantum
470:+noncomputable section
472:+/-! ## Boolean characters -/
474:+/-- The character `a |-> (-1)^(a dot u)` on the Boolean cube `𝔽_2^t`.
476:+This is the scalar character used in the Fourier transform at
477:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`. -/
478:+noncomputable def booleanCharacter {t : ℕ}
479:+    (u a : Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ :=
480:+  MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffVecChar (p := 2) (F := ZMod 2) u a
482:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
483:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: a Boolean character is
484:+multiplicative in its argument. -/
485:+theorem booleanCharacter_add_right {t : ℕ} (u a b : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
486:+    booleanCharacter u (a + b) = booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter u b := by
487:+  exact AddChar.map_add_eq_mul
488:+    (MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffVecChar (p := 2) (F := ZMod 2) u) a b
490:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
491:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: the Boolean pairing defining
492:+the characters is symmetric. -/
493:+theorem booleanCharacter_comm {t : ℕ} (u a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
494:+    booleanCharacter u a = booleanCharacter a u := by
495:+  simp only [booleanCharacter, MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffVecChar_apply]
496:+  have hdot : MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffDotProduct a u =
497:+      MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffDotProduct u a := by
498:+    unfold MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffDotProduct
499:+    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
500:+    intro i _
501:+    exact mul_comm _ _
502:+  rw [hdot]
504:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
505:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: a Boolean character is
506:+multiplicative in its frequency. -/
507:+theorem booleanCharacter_add_left {t : ℕ} (u v a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
508:+    booleanCharacter (u + v) a = booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter v a := by
509:+  rw [booleanCharacter_comm, booleanCharacter_add_right]
510:+  rw [booleanCharacter_comm a u, booleanCharacter_comm a v]
512:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
513:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: a Boolean character takes
514:+the value one at the zero argument. -/
515:+@[simp]
516:+theorem booleanCharacter_zero_right {t : ℕ} (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
517:+    booleanCharacter u 0 = 1 := by
518:+  change MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffVecChar (p := 2) (F := ZMod 2) u 0 = 1
519:+  exact AddChar.map_zero_eq_one _
521:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
522:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: a Boolean character takes
523:+the value one at the zero frequency. -/
524:+@[simp]
525:+theorem booleanCharacter_zero_left {t : ℕ} (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
526:+    booleanCharacter 0 a = 1 := by
527:+  rw [booleanCharacter_comm]
528:+  exact booleanCharacter_zero_right a
530:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
531:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: every Boolean character
532:+takes values whose square is one. -/
533:+theorem booleanCharacter_mul_self {t : ℕ} (u a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
534:+    booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter u a = 1 := by
535:+  rw [← booleanCharacter_add_right]
536:+  have haa : a + a = 0 := by
537:+    ext i
538:+    exact CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero (a i)
539:+  rw [haa, booleanCharacter_zero_right]
541:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
542:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: Boolean characters are real,
543:+hence fixed by complex conjugation. -/
544:+theorem star_booleanCharacter {t : ℕ} (u a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
545:+    star (booleanCharacter u a) = booleanCharacter u a := by
546:+  rcases mul_self_eq_one_iff.mp (booleanCharacter_mul_self u a) with h | h
547:+  · simp [h]
548:+  · simp [h]
550:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
551:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: the unnormalized character
552:+sum vanishes away from frequency zero. -/
553:+theorem sum_booleanCharacter {t : ℕ} (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
554:+    ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a =
555:+      if u = 0 then (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ) else 0 := by
556:+  rw [show (∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a) =
557:+      (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ) *
558:+        𝔼 a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a by
559:+    rw [Fintype.expect_eq_sum_div_card]
560:+    field_simp]
561:+  rw [show (𝔼 a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a) =
562:+      if u = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 by
563:+    simpa [booleanCharacter] using
564:+      (MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.fourier_fact_vector
565:+        (p := 2) (F := ZMod 2) u)]
566:+  split_ifs <;> simp
568:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
569:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: summing a character over
570:+frequencies gives the delta function at zero. -/
571:+theorem sum_booleanCharacter_swap {t : ℕ} (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
572:+    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a =
573:+      if a = 0 then (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ) else 0 := by
574:+  simpa only [booleanCharacter_comm] using sum_booleanCharacter a
576:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
577:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: orthogonality of two Boolean
578:+characters, in the form used by Fourier inversion and Parseval. -/
579:+theorem sum_booleanCharacter_mul {t : ℕ} (a b : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
580:+    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter u b =
581:+      if a = b then (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ) else 0 := by
582:+  rw [← Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun u _ => booleanCharacter_add_right u a b)]
583:+  rw [sum_booleanCharacter_swap]
584:+  have hab : a + b = 0 ↔ a = b := by
585:+    constructor
586:+    · intro h
587:+      have := congrFun h
588:+      funext i
589:+      have hi := this i
590:+      exact (CharTwo.add_eq_zero.mp hi)
591:+    · intro h
592:+      subst b
593:+      ext i
594:+      exact CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero (a i)
595:+  simp only [hab]
597:+/-! ## Operator-valued Fourier analysis -/
599:+/-- The normalized Fourier coefficient of an operator family on the Boolean
600:+cube.  This is `hat A^u = E_a (-1)^(a dot u) A(a)` from
601:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`. -/
602:+noncomputable def operatorFourier {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
603:+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
604:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) : Op ι :=
605:+  ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
606:+    ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • O a
608:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier argument at
609:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1100`: Fourier coefficients of a
610:+Hermitian operator family are Hermitian. -/
611:+theorem operatorFourier_isHermitian {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
612:+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
613:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, (O a).IsHermitian)
614:+    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
615:+    (operatorFourier O u).IsHermitian := by
616:+  rw [Matrix.IsHermitian]
617:+  simp only [operatorFourier, Matrix.conjTranspose_smul,
618:+    Matrix.conjTranspose_sum, star_inv₀, star_natCast]
619:+  congr 1
620:+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
621:+  intro a _
622:+  rw [star_booleanCharacter, (hO a).eq]
624:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier argument at
625:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1100`: Fourier inversion for
626:+operator-valued functions on the Boolean cube. -/
627:+theorem operatorFourier_inversion {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
628:+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
629:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
630:+    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • operatorFourier O u = O a := by
631:+  classical
632:+  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
633:+  have hN : N ≠ 0 := by
634:+    simp [N]
635:+  calc
636:+    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • operatorFourier O u =
637:+        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
638:+          (booleanCharacter u a * N⁻¹ * booleanCharacter u b) • O b := by
639:+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
640:+      intro u _
641:+      simp only [operatorFourier, N, smul_smul, Finset.smul_sum]
642:+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
643:+      intro b _
644:+      rw [mul_assoc]
645:+    _ = ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
646:+          (booleanCharacter u a * N⁻¹ * booleanCharacter u b) • O b := by
647:+      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
648:+    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
649:+          (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
650:+            booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter u b) • O b := by
651:+      rw [Finset.smul_sum]
652:+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
653:+      intro b _
654:+      rw [smul_smul, ← Finset.sum_smul, Finset.mul_sum]
655:+      apply congrArg (fun c : ℂ => c • O b)
656:+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
657:+      intro u _
658:+      ring
659:+    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
660:+          (if a = b then N else 0) • O b := by
661:+      congr 1
662:+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
663:+      intro b _
664:+      rw [sum_booleanCharacter_mul]
665:+    _ = O a := by
666:+      simp [hN]
668:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier argument at
669:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1100`: the matrix-valued Parseval
670:+identity for the Boolean Fourier transform.  The order of the two operator
671:+families is preserved. -/
672:+theorem sum_operatorFourier_mul_operatorFourier {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
673:+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
674:+    (A B : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) :
675:+    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier A u * operatorFourier B u =
676:+      ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
677:+        ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, A a * B a := by
678:+  classical
679:+  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
680:+  calc
681:+    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier A u * operatorFourier B u =
682:+        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, N⁻¹ •
683:+          ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2,
684:+            (booleanCharacter u a • A a) * operatorFourier B u := by
685:+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
686:+      intro u _
687:+      change (N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • A a) *
688:+          operatorFourier B u = _
689:+      rw [smul_mul_assoc, Finset.sum_mul]
690:+    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2,
691:+          (booleanCharacter u a • A a) * operatorFourier B u := by
692:+      rw [Finset.smul_sum]
693:+    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
694:+          (booleanCharacter u a • A a) * operatorFourier B u := by
695:+      congr 1
696:+      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
697:+    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2,
698:+          A a * (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
699:+            booleanCharacter u a • operatorFourier B u) := by
700:+      congr 1
701:+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
702:+      intro a _
703:+      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
704:+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
705:+      intro u _
706:+      rw [smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm]
707:+    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, A a * B a := by
708:+      congr 1
709:+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
710:+      intro a _
711:+      rw [operatorFourier_inversion]
712:+    _ = ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
713:+          ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, A a * B a := by
714:+      rfl
716:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier argument at
717:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1100`: Parseval specialized to the
718:+square of a single operator family. -/
719:+theorem sum_operatorFourier_sq {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
720:+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
721:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) :
722:+    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u =
723:+      ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
724:+        ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, O a * O a :=
725:+  sum_operatorFourier_mul_operatorFourier O O
727:+/-- For a family of binary observables, the squares of the Fourier
728:+coefficients sum to the identity.  This is the Parseval step asserting that
729:+`B^u = (hat A^u)^2` is a POVM in
730:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1096-1100`. -/
731:+theorem sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one {t : ℕ} {ι : Type}
732:+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
733:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι)
734:+    (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
735:+    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u = 1 := by
736:+  rw [sum_operatorFourier_sq]
737:+  simp_rw [(hO _).2]
738:+  rw [Finset.sum_const]
739:+  rw [← Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul ℂ]
740:+  rw [smul_smul]
741:+  simp
743:+/-! ## Observable-distance normalization -/
745:+/-- The effect of a binary projective measurement obtained from an observable.
746:+The two effects are `(1 + O) / 2` and `(1 - O) / 2`. -/
747:+noncomputable def binaryObservableEffect {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
748:+    [DecidableEq ι] (outcome : Bool) (O : Op ι) : Op ι :=
749:+  if outcome then ((2 : ℂ)⁻¹) • (1 - O) else ((2 : ℂ)⁻¹) • (1 + O)
751:+/-- The squared distance between the binary projective measurements associated
752:+with two observables, summed over their two effects.  This is the measurement
753:+distance calculated in `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912`; its relation
754:+to `stateDepDistSq` is recorded in
755:+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
756:+noncomputable def binaryObservableDistSq {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
757:+    [DecidableEq ι] (S T ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
758:+  ∑ outcome : Bool,
759:+    stateDepDistSq (binaryObservableEffect outcome S)
760:+      (binaryObservableEffect outcome T) ρ
762:+/-- The binary-measurement distance is half the state-dependent operator
763:+distance.
765:+**Local fix:** Source equation (3) at
766:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:903-911` ends by identifying the
767:+binary-measurement distance with the state-dependent operator distance of the
768:+two observables; the correct relation carries the factor `1 / 2` proved here.
769:+Documented in
770:+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
771:+theorem binaryObservableDistSq_eq_stateDepDistSq_div_two
772:+    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S T ρ : Op ι) :
773:+    binaryObservableDistSq S T ρ = stateDepDistSq S T ρ / 2 := by
774:+  simp only [binaryObservableDistSq, Fintype.univ_bool, stateDepDistSq,
775:+    binaryObservableEffect, smul_add, Matrix.conjTranspose_sub,
776:+    Finset.mem_singleton, Bool.true_eq_false, not_false_eq_true,
777:+    Finset.sum_insert, reduceIte, Matrix.conjTranspose_smul, star_inv₀,
778:+    star_ofNat, Matrix.conjTranspose_one, Finset.sum_singleton,
779:+    Bool.false_eq_true, Matrix.conjTranspose_add, add_sub_add_left_eq_sub]
780:+  have hminusStar :
781:+      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - Sᴴ) - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - Tᴴ) =
782:+        -((2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (Sᴴ - Tᴴ)) := by
783:+    module
784:+  have hminus :
785:+      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - S) - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - T) =
786:+        -((2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (S - T)) := by
787:+    module
788:+  have hplusStar :
789:+      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • Sᴴ - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • Tᴴ =
790:+        (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (Sᴴ - Tᴴ) := by
791:+    module
792:+  have hplus :
793:+      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • S - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • T =
794:+        (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (S - T) := by
795:+    module
796:+  rw [hminusStar, hminus, hplusStar, hplus]
797:+  simp only [neg_mul, mul_neg, neg_neg, smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul]
798:+  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
799:+  ring
801:+/-- The state-dependent squared distance between binary observables in terms
802:+of their correlation. -/
803:+theorem stateDepDistSq_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation
804:+    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
805:+    (S T ρ : Op ι) (hS : IsBinaryObservable S)
806:+    (hT : IsBinaryObservable T) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef)
807:+    (htrace : Matrix.trace ρ = 1) :
808:+    stateDepDistSq S T ρ =
809:+      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re := by
810:+  have hstar :
811:+      star (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)) = Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ) := by
812:+    calc
813:+      star (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)) = Matrix.trace ((S * T * ρ)ᴴ) := by
814:+        rw [Matrix.trace_conjTranspose]
815:+      _ = Matrix.trace (ρ * T * S) := by
816:+        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hS.1.eq, hT.1.eq, hρ.isHermitian.eq,
817:+          Matrix.mul_assoc]
818:+      _ = Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ) := by
819:+        exact (Matrix.trace_mul_cycle T S ρ).symm
820:+  have hcross :
821:+      (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re = (Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ)).re := by
822:+    have := congrArg Complex.re hstar
823:+    simpa [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] using this
824:+  have hdiff :
825:+      (S - T)ᴴ * (S - T) =
826:+        (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - S * T - T * S := by
827:+    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, hS.1.eq, hT.1.eq]
828:+    calc
829:+      (S - T) * (S - T) = S * S - S * T - T * S + T * T := by
830:+        noncomm_ring
831:+      _ = (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - S * T - T * S := by
832:+        rw [hS.2, hT.2]
833:+        module
834:+  unfold stateDepDistSq
835:+  rw [hdiff]
836:+  simp only [Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.trace_sub, Complex.sub_re]
837:+  rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul, Matrix.trace_smul, htrace]
838:+  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
839:+  rw [hcross]
840:+  ring
842:+/-- The binary-measurement distance is one minus the real state-dependent
843:+correlation. -/
844:+theorem binaryObservableDistSq_eq_one_sub_correlation
845:+    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
846:+    (S T ρ : Op ι) (hS : IsBinaryObservable S)
847:+    (hT : IsBinaryObservable T) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef)
848:+    (htrace : Matrix.trace ρ = 1) :
849:+    binaryObservableDistSq S T ρ =
850:+      1 - (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re := by
851:+  rw [binaryObservableDistSq_eq_stateDepDistSq_div_two,
852:+    stateDepDistSq_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation S T ρ hS hT hρ htrace]
853:+  ring
855:+end

867:+/-!
868:+# Naimark rounding of the Fourier-square POVM
870:+This file carries out the dilation step in the proof of the quantum linearity
871:+theorem of Natarajan and Vidick.  The Fourier-square POVM `B^u = (hat O^u)^2`
872:+of a family of binary observables `O^a`, indexed by the Boolean cube `F_2^t`,
873:+is dilated by the one-measurement Naimark construction of the low individual
874:+degree test to a projective measurement `{C^u}` on the enlarged space
875:+`ι × Option (F_2^t)`, whose compression along the canonical ancillary vector is
876:+again `{B^u}`.  The signed character sums `L^a = ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} C^u` are then
877:+binary observables satisfying the exact linearity `L^a L^b = L^{a+b}`.
879:+The one-measurement Naimark construction produces projectors indexed by
880:+`Option (F_2^t)`: one for each Fourier outcome and one for the residual outcome
881:+`none`.  Discarding the residual projector would destroy the resolution of the
882:+identity on the enlarged space, and with it the multiplicativity of the signed
883:+sums.  It is therefore folded into the zero Fourier outcome: the projector
884:+attached to `u = 0` is the complement of the sum of the projectors attached to
885:+the nonzero outcomes.  Since the Fourier-square effects themselves sum to the
886:+identity, the folded projector still compresses to `B^0`.
888:+## Main definitions and results
890:+* `naimarkAncilla`, `norm_naimarkAncilla`, `ancProj_naimarkAncilla`: the
891:+  canonical ancillary unit vector and its rank-one density.
892:+* `roundedFourierPVM` with `roundedFourierPVM_isProj`,
893:+  `roundedFourierPVM_sum_eq_one`, `roundedFourierPVM_mul_eq_zero_of_ne`, and
894:+  `trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedFourierPVM`: the dilated projective measurement
895:+  and its compression to the Fourier-square POVM.
896:+* `roundedObservable` with `roundedObservable_mul` and
897:+  `roundedObservable_isBinaryObservable`: the exactly linear binary observables.
898:+* `trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedObservable`: the compression of the rounded
899:+  observables, in the form consumed by the averaged distance bound.
901:+## References
903:+Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574, proof of Theorem 10,
904:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1104`: the Naimark dilation of `{B^u}`
905:+is at lines 1099--1100, the observables `𝒜(a) = ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} C^u` at lines
906:+1100--1102, and their exact linearity at lines 1103--1104.  The QPBT paper
907:+quotes the theorem at
908:+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725`, and
909:+the blueprint statement is `thm:linearity` in
910:+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:98-133`.  The one-measurement
911:+Naimark construction reused here is `oneMeasNaimark` in
912:+`MIPStarRE/LDT/MakingMeasurementsProjective/NaimarkOneMeas.lean`, with its data
913:+structure in `MIPStarRE/LDT/MakingMeasurementsProjective/Defs.lean`.
914:+-/
916:+open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
918:+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
920:+open MIPStarRE.LDT
921:+open MIPStarRE.Quantum
922:+open MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective
924:+noncomputable section
926:+/-! ## The canonical ancillary vector -/
928:+/-- The canonical ancillary vector of the Naimark dilation: the basis vector of
929:+the residual index `none` in `Option (F_2^t)`.  This is the pure state `|anc⟩`
930:+of `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1099-1100`; in the one-measurement
931:+Naimark construction it is the initial state `|⊥⟩` of the auxiliary register. -/
932:+def naimarkAncilla (t : ℕ) : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) :=
933:+  EuclideanSpace.single none 1
935:+/-- The canonical ancillary vector is a unit vector. -/
936:+theorem norm_naimarkAncilla (t : ℕ) : ‖naimarkAncilla t‖ = 1 := by
937:+  simp [naimarkAncilla]
939:+/-- The rank-one density `|anc⟩⟨anc|` of the canonical ancillary vector is the
940:+auxiliary projector `|⊥⟩⟨⊥|` of the one-measurement Naimark construction. -/
941:+theorem ancProj_naimarkAncilla (t : ℕ) :
942:+    ancProj (naimarkAncilla t) = naimarkAuxProjector (Fin t → ZMod 2) := by
943:+  ext i j
944:+  cases i <;> cases j <;>
945:+    simp [ancProj, naimarkAncilla, naimarkAuxProjector, Matrix.vecMulVec_apply]
947:+/-! ## The Naimark dilation of the Fourier-square POVM -/
949:+/-- The one-measurement Naimark dilation data of the Fourier-square POVM
950:+`{B^u}`, supplied by `oneMeasNaimark`: a family of projectors on
951:+`ι × Option (F_2^t)`, indexed by `Option (F_2^t)`, summing to at most the
952:+identity and reproducing every expectation value of `{B^u}` in the lifted
953:+state.  This is the projective measurement produced by Naimark's theorem at
954:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1099-1100`, before the residual outcome is
955:+folded into the zero outcome. -/
956:+def fourierNaimarkData {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
957:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
958:+    OneMeasNaimarkData (Fin t → ZMod 2) ι :=
959:+  Classical.choose (oneMeasNaimark (fourierSquareMeasurement O hO).toSubmeasurement)
961:+/-- The Naimark dilation data of `fourierNaimarkData` dilates the Fourier-square
962:+POVM. -/
963:+theorem fourierNaimarkData_source {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
964:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
965:+    (fourierNaimarkData O hO).source = (fourierSquareMeasurement O hO).toSubmeasurement :=
966:+  Classical.choose_spec (oneMeasNaimark (fourierSquareMeasurement O hO).toSubmeasurement)
968:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the rounding below: distinct
969:+projectors of a one-measurement Naimark dilation are orthogonal, since they are
970:+projectors summing to at most the identity. -/
971:+private theorem liftedEffect_mul_liftedEffect_of_ne {α d : Type*}
972:+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
973:+    (data : OneMeasNaimarkData α d) {a b : Option α} (hab : a ≠ b) :
974:+    data.liftedEffect a * data.liftedEffect b = 0 :=
975:+  data.toProjSubMeasOption.outcome_orthogonal a b hab
977:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the compression identities below:
978:+the expectation-preservation identity of a one-measurement Naimark dilation,
979:+written with plain traces.  For every operator `X` on the original space,
980:+`Tr((X ⊗ |⊥⟩⟨⊥|) P̂_a) = Tr(X M_a)`. -/
981:+private theorem trace_kronecker_auxProjector_mul_liftedEffect {α d : Type*}
982:+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
983:+    (data : OneMeasNaimarkData α d) (X : Op d) (a : α) :
984:+    Matrix.trace (Matrix.kronecker X (naimarkAuxProjector α) * data.liftedEffect (some a)) =
985:+      Matrix.trace (X * data.source.effect a) := by
986:+  have h := data.expectation_preservation X a
987:+  simp only [normalizedTrace, oneMeasLiftedDensity, smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul,
988:+    smul_eq_mul, Fintype.card_prod, Nat.cast_mul] at h
989:+  rcases isEmpty_or_nonempty d with hd | hd
990:+  · simp [Matrix.trace]
991:+  · have hd0 : (Fintype.card d : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
992:+    have hα : (Fintype.card (Option α) : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
993:+    rw [mul_comm (Fintype.card d : ℂ), mul_div_mul_left _ _ hα, div_left_inj' hd0] at h
994:+    exact h.symm
996:+/-! ## Folding the residual outcome into the zero Fourier outcome -/
998:+/-- The rounded Fourier projective measurement `{C^u}` on `ι × Option (F_2^t)`,
999:+obtained from the Naimark dilation of the Fourier-square POVM by folding the
1000:+residual outcome `none` into the zero Fourier outcome.  For `u ≠ 0` the
1001:+projector is the dilated projector of the outcome `u`; for `u = 0` it is the
1002:+complement of the sum of the dilated projectors of the nonzero outcomes, so
1003:+that the family resolves the identity on the enlarged space.  This is the
1004:+projective measurement `{C^u}` of `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1099-1100`. -/
1005:+def roundedFourierPVM {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
1006:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
1007:+    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) : Op (ι × Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) :=
1008:+  if u = 0 then
1009:+    1 - ∑ v ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v)
1010:+  else (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some u)
1012:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `roundedFourierPVM`: the sum of the
1013:+dilated projectors of the nonzero Fourier outcomes absorbs each of them on the
1014:+left. -/
1015:+private theorem sum_erase_mul_liftedEffect {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
1016:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
1017:+    {v : Fin t → ZMod 2} (hv : v ≠ 0) :
1018:+    (∑ w ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some w)) *
1019:+        (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v) =
1020:+      (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v) := by
1021:+  rw [Finset.sum_mul, Finset.sum_eq_single v]
1022:+  · exact ((fourierNaimarkData O hO).lifted_isProj (some v)).isIdempotentElem.eq
1023:+  · intro w _ hwv
1024:+    exact liftedEffect_mul_liftedEffect_of_ne _ (fun h => hwv (Option.some_inj.mp h))
1025:+  · intro hv'
1026:+    exact absurd (Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨hv, Finset.mem_univ v⟩) hv'
1028:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `roundedFourierPVM`: the sum of the
1029:+dilated projectors of the nonzero Fourier outcomes is a projector, its summands
1030:+being mutually orthogonal projectors. -/
1031:+private theorem isProj_sum_erase {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
1032:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
1033:+    IsProj (∑ w ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some w)) := by
1034:+  refine { isIdempotentElem := ?_, isSelfAdjoint := ?_ }
1035:+  · unfold IsIdempotentElem
1036:+    rw [Finset.mul_sum]
1037:+    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
1038:+    intro w hw
1039:+    exact sum_erase_mul_liftedEffect O hO (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hw)
1040:+  · rw [isSelfAdjoint_iff, star_sum]
1041:+    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
1042:+    intro w _
1043:+    exact ((fourierNaimarkData O hO).lifted_isProj (some w)).isSelfAdjoint.star_eq
1045:+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `roundedFourierPVM`: the sum of the
1046:+dilated projectors of the nonzero Fourier outcomes absorbs each of them on the
1047:+right, by taking adjoints in the left absorption. -/
1048:+private theorem liftedEffect_mul_sum_erase {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
1049:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
1050:+    {v : Fin t → ZMod 2} (hv : v ≠ 0) :
1051:+    (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v) *
1052:+        (∑ w ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some w)) =
1053:+      (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v) := by
1054:+  have h := congrArg Matrix.conjTranspose (sum_erase_mul_liftedEffect O hO hv)
1055:+  rwa [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, (isProj_sum_erase O hO).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq,
1056:+    ((fourierNaimarkData O hO).lifted_isProj (some v)).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq] at h
1058:+/-- Every rounded Fourier projector is an orthogonal projection. -/
1059:+theorem roundedFourierPVM_isProj {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
1060:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
1061:+    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
1062:+    IsProj (roundedFourierPVM O hO u) := by
1063:+  unfold roundedFourierPVM
1064:+  by_cases hu : u = 0
1065:+  · rw [if_pos hu]
1066:+    exact (isProj_sum_erase O hO).one_sub
1067:+  · rw [if_neg hu]
1068:+    exact (fourierNaimarkData O hO).lifted_isProj (some u)
1070:+/-- The rounded Fourier projectors resolve the identity on the enlarged space. -/
1071:+theorem roundedFourierPVM_sum_eq_one {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
1072:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
1073:+    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, roundedFourierPVM O hO u = 1 := by
1074:+  rw [← Finset.add_sum_erase Finset.univ _ (Finset.mem_univ (0 : Fin t → ZMod 2))]
1075:+  have hrest : ∑ u ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, roundedFourierPVM O hO u =
1076:+      ∑ u ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some u) := by
1077:+    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
1078:+    intro u hu
1079:+    unfold roundedFourierPVM
1080:+    rw [if_neg (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hu)]
1081:+  rw [hrest]
1082:+  unfold roundedFourierPVM
1083:+  rw [if_pos rfl, sub_add_cancel]
1085:+/-- Distinct rounded Fourier projectors are orthogonal.  This is the
1086:+orthogonality of the projectors `C^u` invoked at
1087:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1103-1104`. -/
1088:+theorem roundedFourierPVM_mul_eq_zero_of_ne {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
1089:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
1090:+    {u v : Fin t → ZMod 2} (huv : u ≠ v) :
1091:+    roundedFourierPVM O hO u * roundedFourierPVM O hO v = 0 := by
1092:+  unfold roundedFourierPVM
1093:+  by_cases hu : u = 0 <;> by_cases hv : v = 0
1094:+  · exact absurd (hu.trans hv.symm) huv
1095:+  · rw [if_pos hu, if_neg hv, Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.one_mul,
1096:+      sum_erase_mul_liftedEffect O hO hv, sub_self]
1097:+  · rw [if_neg hu, if_pos hv, Matrix.mul_sub, Matrix.mul_one,
1098:+      liftedEffect_mul_sum_erase O hO hu, sub_self]
1099:+  · rw [if_neg hu, if_neg hv]
1100:+    exact liftedEffect_mul_liftedEffect_of_ne _ (fun h => huv (Option.some_inj.mp h))
1102:+/-- The compression identity of the rounded Fourier projective measurement: for
1103:+every operator `X` on the original space,
1104:+`Tr((X ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|) C^u) = Tr(X B^u)`, where `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` is the
1105:+Fourier-square effect.  For a nonzero outcome this is the expectation
1106:+preservation of the one-measurement Naimark dilation; for the zero outcome it
1107:+follows from the resolution of the identity by the `B^u`.  This is the sense in
1108:+which `{C^u}` simulates `{B^u}` at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1099-1100`. -/
1109:+theorem trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedFourierPVM {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
1110:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
1111:+    (X : Op ι) (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
1112:+    Matrix.trace (heteroKron X (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)) * roundedFourierPVM O hO u) =
1113:+      Matrix.trace (X * (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) := by
1114:+  have hP : ∀ v : Fin t → ZMod 2,
1115:+      Matrix.trace (heteroKron X (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)) *
1116:+          (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v)) =
1117:+        Matrix.trace (X * (operatorFourier O v * operatorFourier O v)) := by
1118:+    intro v
1119:+    rw [ancProj_naimarkAncilla]
1120:+    unfold heteroKron
1121:+    rw [trace_kronecker_auxProjector_mul_liftedEffect, fourierNaimarkData_source]
1122:+    rfl
1123:+  unfold roundedFourierPVM
1124:+  by_cases hu : u = 0
1125:+  · rw [if_pos hu]
1126:+    subst hu
1127:+    have hone :
1128:+        Matrix.trace (heteroKron X (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)) * 1) = Matrix.trace (X * 1) := by
1129:+      rw [Matrix.mul_one, Matrix.mul_one, ancProj_naimarkAncilla]
1130:+      unfold heteroKron naimarkAuxProjector
1131:+      simpa using Matrix.trace_kronecker X
1132:+        (Matrix.single (none : Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) none (1 : ℂ))
1133:+    have hB : X * (operatorFourier O 0 * operatorFourier O 0) =
1134:+        X * 1 - ∑ v ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, X * (operatorFourier O v * operatorFourier O v) := by
1135:+      rw [← Finset.mul_sum, ← Matrix.mul_sub]
1136:+      congr 1
1137:+      rw [eq_sub_iff_add_eq]
1138:+      exact (Finset.add_sum_erase Finset.univ
1139:+        (fun v => operatorFourier O v * operatorFourier O v) (Finset.mem_univ 0)).trans
1140:+        (sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one O hO)
1141:+    rw [hB, Matrix.mul_sub, Finset.mul_sum, Matrix.trace_sub, Matrix.trace_sub,
1142:+      Matrix.trace_sum, Matrix.trace_sum, hone]
1143:+    congr 1
1144:+    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun v _ => hP v)
1145:+  · rw [if_neg hu]
1146:+    exact hP u
1148:+/-! ## The rounded observables -/
1150:+/-- The rounded observables `L^a = ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} C^u`, the signed sums of the
1151:+rounded Fourier projectors.  These are the observables `𝒜(a)` introduced at
1152:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1100-1102`; the character `(-1)^{u·a}` is
1153:+`booleanCharacter u a`. -/
1154:+def roundedObservable {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
1155:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
1156:+    (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) : Op (ι × Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) :=
1157:+  ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • roundedFourierPVM O hO u
1159:+/-- The exact linearity `L^a L^b = L^{a+b}` of the rounded observables, for
1160:+every pair of Boolean-group elements.  Expanding the product, the orthogonality
1161:+and idempotence of the projectors `C^u` leave only the diagonal terms, and the
1162:+characters multiply.  This is the deduction at
1163:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1103-1104`. -/
1164:+theorem roundedObservable_mul {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
1165:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
1166:+    (a b : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
1167:+    roundedObservable O hO a * roundedObservable O hO b = roundedObservable O hO (a + b) := by
1168:+  unfold roundedObservable
1169:+  rw [Finset.sum_mul]
1170:+  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
1171:+  intro u _
1172:+  rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_eq_single u]
1173:+  · rw [smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm, smul_smul,
1174:+      (roundedFourierPVM_isProj O hO u).isIdempotentElem.eq, ← booleanCharacter_add_right]
1175:+  · intro v _ hvu
1176:+    rw [smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm, roundedFourierPVM_mul_eq_zero_of_ne O hO hvu.symm,
1177:+      smul_zero, smul_zero]
1178:+  · intro hu
1179:+    exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ u) hu
1181:+/-- The rounded observable at the zero group element is the identity. -/
1182:+theorem roundedObservable_zero {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
1183:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
1184:+    roundedObservable O hO 0 = 1 := by
1185:+  simp [roundedObservable, roundedFourierPVM_sum_eq_one]
1187:+/-- The rounded observables are Hermitian: the characters are real and the
1188:+rounded Fourier projectors are self-adjoint. -/
1189:+theorem roundedObservable_isHermitian {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
1190:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
1191:+    (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
1192:+    (roundedObservable O hO a).IsHermitian := by
1193:+  rw [Matrix.IsHermitian, roundedObservable, Matrix.conjTranspose_sum]
1194:+  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
1195:+  intro u _
1196:+  rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_smul, star_booleanCharacter,
1197:+    (roundedFourierPVM_isProj O hO u).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq]
1199:+/-- Every rounded observable is a binary observable: it is Hermitian, and its
1200:+square is `L^{a+a} = L^0 = 1` by exact linearity. -/
1201:+theorem roundedObservable_isBinaryObservable {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
1202:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
1203:+    (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
1204:+    IsBinaryObservable (roundedObservable O hO a) := by
1205:+  refine ⟨roundedObservable_isHermitian O hO a, ?_⟩
1206:+  have haa : a + a = 0 := by
1207:+    ext i
1208:+    exact CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero (a i)
1209:+  rw [roundedObservable_mul, haa, roundedObservable_zero]
1211:+/-- The compression identity of the rounded observables: for every operator `X`
1212:+on the original space,
1213:+`Tr((X ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|) L^a) = Tr(X ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} B^u)`.  The right-hand side
1214:+is the character sum of the Fourier-square POVM whose overlap with `O^a` is
1215:+certified by `one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare`; this is the passage
1216:+from `Tr_{ρ'}(A(a) 𝒜(a))` to `Tr_ρ(A(a) ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} (hat A^u)^2)` at
1217:+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1105-1110`. -/
1218:+theorem trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedObservable {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
1219:+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
1220:+    (X : Op ι) (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
1221:+    Matrix.trace (heteroKron X (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)) * roundedObservable O hO a) =
1222:+      Matrix.trace (X * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a •
1223:+        (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) := by
1224:+  simp only [roundedObservable, Finset.mul_sum, Matrix.trace_sum, mul_smul_comm,
1225:+    Matrix.trace_smul, trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedFourierPVM]
1227:+end

1235:+\begin{remark}[Normalization of the distance in the linearity conclusion]
1236:+	\label{rem:linearity-distance-normalization}
1237:+	The conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} bounds the state-dependent
1238:+	operator distance $d_{\rho'}$ by $\delta$, as quoted in
1239:+	\cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. The calculation behind that bound in
1240:+	\cite[Section~3.1]{Natarajan2017Linearity} computes the distance between
1241:+	the binary projective measurements associated with the observables, which
1242:+	is half the squared operator distance, and then identifies the two
1243:+	quantities; the identification loses that factor. What the Fourier
1244:+	argument proves is the bound $\delta$ for the squared measurement
1245:+	distance, equivalently $2\delta$ for the squared operator distance, and
1246:+	the operator bound $\delta$ stated above is refuted by a four-point
1247:+	counterexample \cite{gap:qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization}. The
1248:+	normalization identities are recorded in
1249:+	Lemma~\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance}; realigning the statement of
1250:+	Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} is a separate task.
1251:+\end{remark}
1253:+\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for the Boolean Fourier transform]
1254:+	\label{lem:boolean-fourier-transform}
1255:+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.booleanCharacter, MIPStarRE.QPBT.operatorFourier}
1256:+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.operatorFourier_isHermitian}
1257:+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.operatorFourier_inversion}
1258:+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.sum_operatorFourier_mul_operatorFourier}
1259:+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one}
1260:+	\leanok
1261:+	This is not a named statement of \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}; it isolates
1262:+	the finite Fourier identities used in the proof given there for
1263:+	Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity}. Write $\chi_u(a) = (-1)^{u \cdot a}$ for
1264:+	$u, a \in \F_2^t$ and, for a family $\{O(a)\}_{a \in \F_2^t}$ of operators,
1265:+	set $\widehat{O}^u = \E_a \, \chi_u(a) \, O(a)$. Each $\widehat{O}^u$ is
1266:+	Hermitian when every $O(a)$ is, and for two such families $A$ and $B$,
1267:+	\[
1268:+		O(a) = \sum_u \chi_u(a) \, \widehat{O}^u ,
1269:+		\qquad
1270:+		\sum_u \widehat{A}^u \, \widehat{B}^u = \E_a \, A(a) B(a) .
1271:+	\]
1272:+	If every $O(a)$ is a binary observable, then
1273:+	$\sum_u (\widehat{O}^u)^2 = \Id$.
1274:+\end{lemma}
1275:+\begin{proof}
1276:+	\leanok
1277:+	Orthogonality of the characters of $\F_2^t$ gives the inversion formula;
1278:+	the Parseval identity follows by substituting it into the product and
1279:+	exchanging the two sums; the last identity uses $O(a)^2 = \Id$.
1280:+\end{proof}
1282:+\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for the binary-measurement distance]
1283:+	\label{lem:binary-measurement-distance}
1284:+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.binaryObservableEffect}
1285:+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.binaryObservableDistSq}
1286:+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.binaryObservableDistSq_eq_stateDepDistSq_div_two}
1287:+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.stateDepDistSq_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation}
1288:+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.binaryObservableDistSq_eq_one_sub_correlation}
1289:+	\leanok
1290:+	\uses{def:povm-conventions}
1291:+	This is not a named statement of \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}; it records
1292:+	the normalization discussed in
1293:+	Remark~\ref{rem:linearity-distance-normalization}. Let $S$ and $T$ be
1294:+	binary observables, let $\rho$ be a density operator, write
1295:+	$P_S^\pm = (\Id \pm S)/2$ for the effects of the associated binary
1296:+	projective measurements, and set
1297:+	$d^{\mathrm{bin}}_\rho(S,T)^2
1298:+	= \sum_{s \in \{+,-\}} d_\rho(P_S^s, P_T^s)^2$. Then
1299:+	\[
1300:+		d^{\mathrm{bin}}_\rho(S,T)^2 = \tfrac{1}{2} \, d_\rho(S,T)^2 ,
1301:+		\quad
1302:+		d_\rho(S,T)^2 = 2 - 2 \Re \Tr(S T \rho) ,
1303:+		\quad
1304:+		d^{\mathrm{bin}}_\rho(S,T)^2 = 1 - \Re \Tr(S T \rho) .
1305:+	\]
1306:+\end{lemma}
1307:+\begin{proof}
1308:+	\leanok
1309:+	Expand $P_S^s - P_T^s = \pm (S - T)/2$ in each of the two outcomes and
1310:+	sum. The remaining identities use $S^2 = T^2 = \Id$, $\Tr \rho = 1$, and
1311:+	the Hermiticity of $S$, $T$ and $\rho$.
1312:+\end{proof}

     4	/-!
     5	# Naimark rounding of the Fourier-square POVM
     6	
     7	This file carries out the dilation step in the proof of the quantum linearity
     8	theorem of Natarajan and Vidick.  The Fourier-square POVM `B^u = (hat O^u)^2`
     9	of a family of binary observables `O^a`, indexed by the Boolean cube `F_2^t`,
    10	is dilated by the one-measurement Naimark construction of the low individual
    11	degree test to a projective measurement `{C^u}` on the enlarged space
    12	`ι × Option (F_2^t)`, whose compression along the canonical ancillary vector is
    13	again `{B^u}`.  The signed character sums `L^a = ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} C^u` are then
    14	binary observables satisfying the exact linearity `L^a L^b = L^{a+b}`.
    15	
    16	The one-measurement Naimark construction produces projectors indexed by
    17	`Option (F_2^t)`: one for each Fourier outcome and one for the residual outcome
    18	`none`.  Discarding the residual projector would destroy the resolution of the
    19	identity on the enlarged space, and with it the multiplicativity of the signed
    20	sums.  It is therefore folded into the zero Fourier outcome: the projector
    21	attached to `u = 0` is the complement of the sum of the projectors attached to
    22	the nonzero outcomes.  Since the Fourier-square effects themselves sum to the
    23	identity, the folded projector still compresses to `B^0`.
    24	
    25	## Main definitions and results
    26	
    27	* `naimarkAncilla`, `norm_naimarkAncilla`, `ancProj_naimarkAncilla`: the
    28	  canonical ancillary unit vector and its rank-one density.
    29	* `roundedFourierPVM` with `roundedFourierPVM_isProj`,
    30	  `roundedFourierPVM_sum_eq_one`, `roundedFourierPVM_mul_eq_zero_of_ne`, and
    31	  `trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedFourierPVM`: the dilated projective measurement
    32	  and its compression to the Fourier-square POVM.
    33	* `roundedObservable` with `roundedObservable_mul` and
    34	  `roundedObservable_isBinaryObservable`: the exactly linear binary observables.
    35	* `trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedObservable`: the compression of the rounded
    36	  observables, in the form consumed by the averaged distance bound.
    37	
    38	## References
    39	
    40	Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574, proof of Theorem 10,
    41	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1104`: the Naimark dilation of `{B^u}`
    42	is at lines 1099--1100, the observables `𝒜(a) = ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} C^u` at lines
    43	1100--1102, and their exact linearity at lines 1103--1104.  The QPBT paper
    44	quotes the theorem at
    45	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725`, and
    46	the blueprint statement is `thm:linearity` in
    47	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:98-133`.  The one-measurement
    48	Naimark construction reused here is `oneMeasNaimark` in
    49	`MIPStarRE/LDT/MakingMeasurementsProjective/NaimarkOneMeas.lean`, with its data
    50	structure in `MIPStarRE/LDT/MakingMeasurementsProjective/Defs.lean`.
    51	-/

    63	/-! ## The canonical ancillary vector -/
    64	
    65	/-- The canonical ancillary vector of the Naimark dilation: the basis vector of
    66	the residual index `none` in `Option (F_2^t)`.  This is the pure state `|anc⟩`
    67	of `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1099-1100`; in the one-measurement
    68	Naimark construction it is the initial state `|⊥⟩` of the auxiliary register. -/
    69	def naimarkAncilla (t : ℕ) : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) :=
    70	  EuclideanSpace.single none 1
    71	
    72	/-- The canonical ancillary vector is a unit vector. -/
    73	theorem norm_naimarkAncilla (t : ℕ) : ‖naimarkAncilla t‖ = 1 := by
    74	  simp [naimarkAncilla]
    75	
    76	/-- The rank-one density `|anc⟩⟨anc|` of the canonical ancillary vector is the

     4	/-!
     5	# The operator-valued BLR bound
     6	
     7	This file carries out the Fourier-analytic part of the proof of the quantum
     8	linearity theorem of Natarajan and Vidick.  Given binary observables `O^u`
     9	indexed by the Boolean cube `(ZMod 2)^t` and a positive semidefinite trace-one
    10	operator `ρ`, it expresses the state-dependent multiplicative defect of the
    11	family through the two-query correlation of the linearity test, identifies the
    12	sum of the cubic Fourier coefficients with that correlation, and records the
    13	overlap certificate for the Fourier-square POVM `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` that the
    14	Naimark dilation consumes.  Pairwise commutation of the observables is never
    15	assumed, and every complex trace is handled through its real part.
    16	
    17	## Main results
    18	
    19	* `multiplicativeDefect`: the state-dependent squared defect of `O^u O^v`
    20	  from `O^{u+v}`.
    21	* `avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation` and
    22	  `avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error`: the average defect equals
    23	  `2 - 2 * (correlation)`, hence is at most `2 * δ` under the correlation
    24	  hypothesis of `exists_exactly_linear_observables`.
    25	* `operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation`: the identity
    26	  `∑_u Tr_ρ((hat O^u)^3) = E_{a,b} Tr_ρ(O^a O^b O^{a+b})`.
    27	* `fourierSquareMeasurement` and `one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare`:
    28	  the Fourier-square POVM together with its overlap certificate.
    29	
    30	## References
    31	
    32	Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574, Theorem 10 with displays (7)--(8) and
    33	its proof, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1113`; the state-dependent
    34	distance is defined at lines 866--900 of the same file.  The QPBT paper quotes
    35	the theorem at
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725` and
    37	invokes it at lines 787--832.  The blueprint statement is `thm:linearity` in
    38	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:81-147`.  The normalization of
    39	the error constant is analyzed in
    40	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`: the exact defect
    41	bound is `2 * δ` for the raw distance `stateDepDistSq`, equivalently `δ` for
    42	the normalized binary-observable distance.
    43	-/
    44	
    45	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    46

    54	/-! ## The two-query correlation and the multiplicative defect -/
    55	
    56	/-- The two-query correlation of the linearity test: the average, over a
    57	uniformly random pair `(u, u')` in `(ZMod 2)^t`, of the real part of
    58	`Tr(O^u O^{u'} O^{u+u'} ρ)`.  This is the left-hand side of display (7) in
    59	Natarajan--Vidick, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`, and the
    60	quantity bounded below in the hypothesis of
    61	`exists_exactly_linear_observables`; the order of the two uniform variables is
    62	the one used there. -/
    63	def blrCorrelation {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    64	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
    65	  avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
    66	    (fun pair =>
    67	      (Matrix.trace (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)
    68	
    69	/-- The state-dependent squared defect of the product `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}`,
    70	namely `d_ρ(O^u O^v, O^{u+v})^2` for the state-dependent distance of
    71	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:873-875`.  Its average over uniformly random
    72	`u, v` is the approximate-linearity error of the family in the sense of the QPBT
    73	quotation `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`,
    74	measured with the raw distance `stateDepDistSq`. -/
    75	def multiplicativeDefect {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    76	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℝ :=
    77	  stateDepDistSq (O u * O v) (O (u + v)) ρ
    78	
    79	/-- Pointwise form of the defect identity: for binary observables the squared
    80	defect of `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}` is `2 - 2 Re Tr(O^v O^u O^{v+u} ρ)`.  The
    81	expansion of `(O^u O^v - O^{u+v})^† (O^u O^v - O^{u+v})` produces the two
    82	triple products `O^v O^u O^{u+v}` and `O^{u+v} O^u O^v`; the second is the
    83	adjoint of the first, so their traces against `ρ` are complex conjugates with
    84	equal real parts.  This is the calculation behind display (3) of
    85	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912`, applied to the products of the
    86	family. -/
    87	theorem multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
    88	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    89	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
    90	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
    91	    (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    92	    multiplicativeDefect O ρ u v =
    93	      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (v + u) * ρ)).re := by
    94	  have hu := hO u
    95	  have hv := hO v
    96	  have huv := hO (u + v)
    97	  have hdiff :
    98	      (O u * O v - O (u + v))ᴴ * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
    99	        (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) - O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
   100	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq,
   101	      huv.1.eq]
   102	    calc
   103	      (O v * O u - O (u + v)) * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
   104	          O v * (O u * O u) * O v - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
   105	            O (u + v) * O u * O v + O (u + v) * O (u + v) := by
   106	        noncomm_ring
   107	      _ = (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
   108	            O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
   109	        rw [hu.2, Matrix.mul_one, hv.2, huv.2]
   110	        module
   111	  have hstar :
   112	      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
   113	        Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
   114	    calc
   115	      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
   116	          Matrix.trace ((O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)ᴴ) := by
   117	        rw [Matrix.trace_conjTranspose]
   118	      _ = Matrix.trace (ρ * (O v * O u * O (u + v))) := by
   119	        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq, huv.1.eq,
   120	          hρ.isHermitian.eq, Matrix.mul_assoc]
   121	      _ = Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
   122	        exact Matrix.trace_mul_comm _ _
   123	  have hcross :
   124	      (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)).re =
   125	        (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ)).re := by
   126	    have := congrArg Complex.re hstar
   127	    simpa [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] using this
   128	  unfold multiplicativeDefect stateDepDistSq
   129	  rw [hdiff]
   130	  simp only [Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.trace_sub, Complex.sub_re]
   131	  rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul, Matrix.trace_smul, htrace]
   132	  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
   133	  rw [hcross, add_comm v u]
   134	  ring
