   136	/-- The average multiplicative defect over a uniformly random pair equals
   137	`2 - 2 * (two-query correlation)`.  The pointwise identity
   138	`multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation` produces the correlation
   139	summand with the two variables in reversed order; since the pair is uniform,
   140	exchanging the two coordinates leaves the average unchanged.  This is the
   141	relation between the approximate-linearity hypothesis of the QPBT quotation
   142	(`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`) and
   143	display (7) of Natarajan--Vidick (`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`),
   144	in the raw normalization of
   145	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   146	theorem avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
   147	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   148	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   149	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1) :
   150	    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   151	        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) =
   152	      2 - 2 * blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   153	  have hswap :
   154	      avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   155	        (fun pair =>
   156	          (Matrix.trace (O pair.2 * O pair.1 * O (pair.2 + pair.1) * ρ)).re) =
   157	        blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   158	    unfold blrCorrelation
   159	    refine (avgOver_uniform_equiv (Equiv.prodComm _ _) _).trans ?_
   160	    exact avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun pair => rfl)
   161	  calc
   162	    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   163	        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) =
   164	        avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   165	          (fun pair => 2 - 2 *
   166	            (Matrix.trace (O pair.2 * O pair.1 * O (pair.2 + pair.1) * ρ)).re) :=
   167	      avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun pair =>
   168	        multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation O hO ρ hρ htrace
   169	          pair.1 pair.2)
   170	    _ = 2 - 2 * blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   171	      rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_mul, avgOver_uniform_const, hswap]
   172	
   173	/-- The operator-valued BLR bound: under the correlation hypothesis of
   174	`exists_exactly_linear_observables`, the average squared defect of `O^u O^v`
   175	from `O^{u+v}` is at most `2 * δ`.  This is the passage from display (7) of
   176	Natarajan--Vidick (`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`) to the
   177	approximate-linearity relation of the QPBT quotation
   178	(`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`); the
   179	constant `2` is the raw-distance normalization recorded in
   180	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   181	theorem avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error {t : ℕ}
   182	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   183	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   184	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
   185	    (δ : ℝ) (hcorrelation : 1 - δ ≤ blrCorrelation O ρ) :
   186	    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   187	        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) ≤ 2 * δ := by
   188	  rw [avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation O hO ρ hρ htrace]

   192	
   193	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier computations in the
   194	proof of Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick
   195	(`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1096-1112`): a twisted form of the
   196	matrix-valued Parseval identity in which only the first factor is expanded
   197	through its Fourier coefficients.  Taking `a = 0` recovers Parseval. -/
   198	private theorem sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul {t : ℕ}
   199	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   200	    (A X : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   230	      intro b _
   231	      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   232	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   233	      intro u _
   234	      rw [mul_smul_comm]
   235	
   236	/-- The sum of the cubes of the Fourier coefficients of an operator family is
   237	the average of `O^a O^b O^{a+b}` over a uniformly random pair `(a, b)`.  This
   238	is the operator form of the identity
   239	`∑_u (hat A^u)^3 = E_{a,b} A(a) A(b) A(a+b)` invoked at
   240	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1111-1112`; the order of the three factors
   241	is preserved throughout. -/
   242	theorem sum_operatorFourier_cube {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   243	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) :
   244	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   245	        operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u =
   246	      ((Fintype.card ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   247	        ∑ p : (Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2),
   248	          O p.1 * O p.2 * O (p.1 + p.2) := by
   249	  classical
   250	  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
   251	  have hinner : ∀ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   252	      ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   253	          booleanCharacter u b • (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) =
   254	        N⁻¹ • ∑ c : Fin t → ZMod 2, O c * O (b + c) := by
   255	    intro b
   256	    rw [sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul]
   257	    congr 1
   258	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   259	    intro c _
   260	    rw [operatorFourier_inversion]
   261	  calc
   262	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   263	        operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u =
   264	        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u 0 •
   265	          (operatorFourier O u * (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) := by
   266	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   267	      intro u _
   268	      rw [booleanCharacter_zero_right, one_smul, Matrix.mul_assoc]
   269	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, O b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   270	          booleanCharacter u (0 + b) •
   271	            (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) := by
   272	      rw [sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul]
   273	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   274	          O b * (N⁻¹ • ∑ c : Fin t → ZMod 2, O c * O (b + c)) := by
   275	      simp only [zero_add, hinner]
   276	    _ = (N⁻¹ * N⁻¹) • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ c : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   277	          O b * O c * O (b + c) := by
   278	      simp only [mul_smul_comm, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.smul_sum, smul_smul,
   279	        Matrix.mul_assoc]
   280	    _ = ((Fintype.card ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   281	          ∑ p : (Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2),
   282	            O p.1 * O p.2 * O (p.1 + p.2) := by
   283	      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type, Fintype.card_prod, Nat.cast_mul, mul_inv]
   284	
   285	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the averages in this file: a uniform

   312	/-! ## The Fourier-square POVM and its overlap certificate -/
   313	
   314	/-- Each Fourier square `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` of a Hermitian operator family is
   315	positive semidefinite, being the product of a Hermitian matrix with its
   316	adjoint.  This is the positivity half of the assertion that the `B^u` form a
   317	POVM at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1098-1099`. -/
   318	theorem operatorFourier_mul_self_posSemidef {t : ℕ}
   319	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   320	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, (O a).IsHermitian)
   321	    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   322	    (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u).PosSemidef := by
   323	  have h := operatorFourier_isHermitian O hO u
   324	  simpa [h.eq] using
   325	    Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self (operatorFourier O u)

   331	theorem is applied at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1097-1100`. -/

   336	    (fun u => operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)
   337	    (fun u => (operatorFourier_mul_self_posSemidef O (fun a => (hO a).1) u).nonneg)
   338	    (sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one O hO)

   342	@[simp]

   344	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   345	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   346	    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   347	    (fourierSquareMeasurement O hO).effect u =

   349	  rfl

   354	`E_a Re Tr_{ρ'}(A(a) 𝒜(a))` at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1104-1110`,

   356	of the exactly linear observable `𝒜(a) = ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} C^u` to the original

   358	theorem avg_overlap_fourierSquare_eq_sum_cube {t : ℕ}
   359	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   360	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) :
   361	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
   362	        (fun a => (Matrix.trace (O a *
   363	          (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a •
   364	            (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) * ρ)).re) =
   365	      ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   366	        (Matrix.trace (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u *
   367	          operatorFourier O u * ρ)).re := by
   368	  classical
   369	  have hop :
   370	      ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   371	          operatorFourier O u * (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) =
   372	        ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   373	          ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, O b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   374	            booleanCharacter u b • (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) := by
   375	    have := sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul O
   376	      (fun u => operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) 0
   377	    simpa only [booleanCharacter_zero_right, one_smul, zero_add] using this
   378	  symm
   379	  calc
   380	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   381	        (Matrix.trace (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u *
   382	          operatorFourier O u * ρ)).re =
   383	        (Matrix.trace ((∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   384	          operatorFourier O u * (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) *
   385	            ρ)).re := by
   386	      rw [Finset.sum_mul, Matrix.trace_sum, Complex.re_sum]
   387	      simp only [Matrix.mul_assoc]
   388	    _ = (Matrix.trace ((((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   389	          ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, O b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   390	            booleanCharacter u b • (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) *

    56	
    57	If `V†V = P` where `P` is a projection and `V = VP`, then there exists

    61	isometry from range(P) to V's range, and in finite dimensions any
    62	isometry between subspaces extends to a unitary.

    76	  have toEuclideanLin_mul :

    80	    intro A B
    81	    simp [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_mul_same (p := (2 : ENNReal)) A B]
    82	  let Pₗ : EuclideanSpace ℂ n →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n := Matrix.toEuclideanLin P
    83	  let Vₗ : EuclideanSpace ℂ n →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n := Matrix.toEuclideanLin V

    87	    intro x

    89	    rw [← hy]
    90	    calc
    91	      Pₗ (Pₗ y) = (Pₗ.comp Pₗ) y := rfl
    92	      _ = Matrix.toEuclideanLin (P * P) y := by rw [toEuclideanLin_mul]

    95	    calc
    96	      Vₗ.comp Pₗ = Matrix.toEuclideanLin (V * P) := by rw [toEuclideanLin_mul]

    98	  have hgram : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) = Pₗ := by
    99	    calc
   100	      Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) = Matrix.toEuclideanLin P := by rw [hVV]
   101	      _ = Pₗ := rfl
   102	  let Llin : S →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n := Vₗ.comp S.subtype
   103	  have hLnorm : ∀ x : S, ‖Llin x‖ = ‖x‖ := by
   104	    exact (LinearMap.norm_map_iff_inner_map_map
   105	      (𝕜 := ℂ) (E := S) (E' := EuclideanSpace ℂ n)
   106	      (F := S →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n) Llin).2 fun x y => by
   107	      have hy : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) = y := by
   108	        calc
   109	          Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) =
   110	              Pₗ (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) := by rw [hgram]

   112	      calc
   113	        inner ℂ (Llin x) (Llin y) =
   114	            inner ℂ (Vₗ (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)) (Vₗ (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)) := rfl

   116	            (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)) := by
   117	          dsimp [Vₗ]
   118	          rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_mul_self]

   121	            (Matrix.toEuclideanLin V (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n))).symm

   129	  have hUmat_lin : Matrix.toEuclideanLin Umat = Ulin.toLinearMap := by

   132	    apply Matrix.toEuclideanLin.injective

   136	            rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_mul_self]
   137	      _ = Ulin.toLinearMap.adjoint.comp Ulin.toLinearMap := by rw [hUmat_lin]

   217	/-- **One-measurement Naimark lemma** (Lemma 5.2).
   218	
   219	For any submeasurement `M : Submeasurement α d`, there exists a projective
   220	submeasurement on the enlarged space `d × Option α` such that for every
   221	operator `ρ` on `Op d` and outcome `a`:
   222	`τ(ρ · M_a) = τ'(ρ_lifted · P̂_a)`
   223	where `ρ_lifted = |Option α| · (ρ ⊗ |⊥⟩⟨⊥|)` and `P̂_a` is the
   224	dilated projector.
   225	
   226	**Proof sketch**: Let `V|ψ⟩ = ∑_a √M_a|ψ⟩ ⊗ |a⟩ + √(I−M)|ψ⟩ ⊗ |⊥⟩`.
   227	This is an isometry (by the submeasurement property `∑ M_a ≤ I`).
   228	Define `P̂_a = V†(I ⊗ |a⟩⟨a|)V`. Then `P̂_a` is an orthogonal projection
   229	(since `|a⟩⟨a|` is), and the compression identity
   230	`(I⊗⟨⊥|) P̂_a (I⊗|⊥⟩) = √M_a · √M_a = M_a` gives the result.

   232	The proof uses `CFC.sqrt` for PSD operators together with lemmas such as
   233	`CFC.sqrt_mul_sqrt_self`. -/

   235	    {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   236	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement α d) :
   237	    OneMeasNaimarkLemma α d M := by
   238	  classical
   239	  let auxProj : Option α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α) :=
   240	    fun oa => Matrix.single oa oa 1
   241	  /-
   242	  The prescribed Naimark isometry column:
   243	    `V (|ψ⟩ ⊗ |⊥⟩)
   244	      = ∑_a √(M_a)|ψ⟩ ⊗ |a⟩ + √(I - ∑_a M_a)|ψ⟩ ⊗ |⊥⟩`,
   245	  encoded by `oneMeasNaimarkColumn M`.  Concretely, this matrix is
   246	  supported only on the input `none = ⊥` slice.
   247	  -/
   248	  let V : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (d × Option α) := oneMeasNaimarkColumn M
   249	  /-
   250	  Extend the isometry column `V` to a unitary `U` on the whole enlarged space.
   251	  The dilated projectors are then `U† (I ⊗ |oa⟩⟨oa|) U`.
   252	  -/
   253	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ :=
   254	    partialIsometry_to_unitary
   255	      (oneMeasNaimarkColumn M) (oneMeasNaimarkInputProj (α := α) (d := d))

   257	      (oneMeasNaimarkColumn_mul_inputProj M)

   261	    source := M
   262	    liftedEffect := fun oa =>
   263	      Umatᴴ * Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (auxProj oa) * Umat

+\begin{remark}[Normalization of the distance in the linearity conclusion]
+	\label{rem:linearity-distance-normalization}
+	The conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} bounds the state-dependent
+	operator distance $d_{\rho'}$ by $\delta$, as quoted in
+	\cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. The calculation behind that bound in
+	\cite[Section~3.1]{Natarajan2017Linearity} computes the distance between
+	the binary projective measurements associated with the observables, which
+	is half the squared operator distance, and then identifies the two
+	quantities; the identification loses that factor. What the Fourier
+	argument proves is the bound $\delta$ for the squared measurement
+	distance, equivalently $2\delta$ for the squared operator distance, and
+	the operator bound $\delta$ stated above is refuted by a four-point
+	counterexample \cite{gap:qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization}. The
+	normalization identities are recorded in
+	Lemma~\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance}; realigning the statement of
+	Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} is a separate task.
+\end{remark}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for the Boolean Fourier transform]
+	\label{lem:boolean-fourier-transform}
+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.booleanCharacter, MIPStarRE.QPBT.operatorFourier}
+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.operatorFourier_isHermitian}
+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.operatorFourier_inversion}
+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.sum_operatorFourier_mul_operatorFourier}
+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one}
+	\leanok
+	This is not a named statement of \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}; it isolates
+	the finite Fourier identities used in the proof given there for
+	Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity}. Write $\chi_u(a) = (-1)^{u \cdot a}$ for
+	$u, a \in \F_2^t$ and, for a family $\{O(a)\}_{a \in \F_2^t}$ of operators,
+	set $\widehat{O}^u = \E_a \, \chi_u(a) \, O(a)$. Each $\widehat{O}^u$ is
+	Hermitian when every $O(a)$ is, and for two such families $A$ and $B$,
+	\[
+		O(a) = \sum_u \chi_u(a) \, \widehat{O}^u ,
+		\qquad
+		\sum_u \widehat{A}^u \, \widehat{B}^u = \E_a \, A(a) B(a) .
+	\]
+	If every $O(a)$ is a binary observable, then
+	$\sum_u (\widehat{O}^u)^2 = \Id$.
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+	\leanok
+	Orthogonality of the characters of $\F_2^t$ gives the inversion formula;
+	the Parseval identity follows by substituting it into the product and
+	exchanging the two sums; the last identity uses $O(a)^2 = \Id$.
+\end{proof}

+	\label{lem:binary-measurement-distance}

docs/blueprint_style_guide.md:179:**Proof-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside the matching `proof` environment, preferably as the first line after `\begin{proof}`. The canonical current placement is the theorem `thm:commutativity-points` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch08_commutativity.tex:8-19`, where the statement block has `\leanok` immediately after `\lean{...}` and the proof block begins with another `\leanok`. This marker says that the Lean proof is complete and free of unresolved `sorry` or unjustified project-level `axiom` shortcuts. In particular, `#print axioms <decl>` must show no `sorryAx`, and the declaration must satisfy the broader blocker rules in the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and [`docs/project_conventions.md`](project_conventions.md).
docs/blueprint_style_guide.md:198:**Current CI behavior.** The advisory Blueprint ↔ Lean sync check in [`docs/ci-blueprint-sync.md`](ci-blueprint-sync.md) distinguishes the two placements. Only proof-level `\leanok` whose axiom closure contains `sorryAx` (or whose harness output cannot be parsed) is reported as an **error**. Statement-level-only `\leanok` with the same finding is downgraded to a **warning**, because statement-level does not claim proof completeness. Each audit line is annotated with the observed placement so reviewers can tell statement-sync work apart from proof-completion work.

   756	\begin{lemma}[The sub-line distribution]
   757		\label{lem:qld-sublines}
   758		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.SubLineWitness, MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_subLineWitness}
   759		\notready
   760		\uses{def:line, def:line-point-dist, def:ith-restricted-line}
   761		% Statement as in the source (references/qpbt-paper/
   762		% 14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex, lem:qld-sublines). The
   763		% line-point distribution over F_q^{2m+2} is built from the index
   764		% function chi of def:ld-question-distribution at dimension 2m+2, which
   765		% is defined only when 2m+2 divides q; the source instantiates it
   766		% without securing this condition. See rem:qld-4-7-divisibility.
   767		There exists a distribution $D$
   768		over tuples $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z)$, where $\ell$ is a line in
   769		$\F_q^{2m+2}$ and $\ell_X, \ell_Z$ are lines in $\F_q^m$, with the
   770		following properties:
   771		\begin{enumerate}
   772			\item The marginal distribution over $\ell$ is the same as the
   773			marginal of the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$.
   774			% The source phrases the next property as: the marginal over
   775			% (ell_X, ell_Z) is "a mixture of the product distributions
   776			% D_{ALine,i} x D_{ALine,j} and D_{DLine,i} x D_{DLine,j}". Those
   777			% products are distributions over pairs of line-point pairs, not
   778			% over pairs of lines, so the phrase does not define the asserted
   779			% marginal distribution on pairs of lines as written; the
   780			% formulation below states the mixture at the level of the joint
   781			% law of (ell_X, ell_Z, u), which is what the proofs of
   782			% lem:claim-17-2 and lem:claim-17-3 use.
   783			\item For any point of the form $u = (u_X, u_Z, \alpha, \beta)$
   784			lying on $\ell$, it holds that $u_X \in \ell_X$ and
   785			$u_Z \in \ell_Z$. Moreover, the joint distribution of
   786			$(\ell_X, \ell_Z, u)$, for $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z) \sim D$ and
   787			$u$ chosen uniformly at random on $\ell$, is a mixture of
   788			components indexed by a type
   789			$\mathrm{v} \in \{\mathrm{ALine}, \mathrm{DLine}\}$ and indices
   790			$i, j \in \{1, \dots, m\}$ with the following two properties
   791			within the component $(\mathrm{v}, i, j)$: the pair
   792			$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is distributed according to the product of the
   793			marginal distributions on lines of $D_{\mathrm{v},i}$ and of
   794			$D_{\mathrm{v},j}$, and, conditioned on $(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$, the
   795			point $u_X$ is uniformly distributed on $\ell_X$ and likewise the
   796			point $u_Z$ is uniformly distributed on $\ell_Z$. Equivalently,
   797			since under each restricted distribution the point is uniformly
   798			distributed on the line conditionally on the line: within the
   799			component $(\mathrm{v}, i, j)$, the pair
   800			$((\ell_X, u_X), (\ell_Z, z'))$, where $z'$ is a uniformly random
   801			point of $\ell_Z$ sampled independently of $u$, is distributed
   802			according to $D_{\mathrm{v},i} \times D_{\mathrm{v},j}$, and
   803			symmetrically the pair $((\ell_X, x'), (\ell_Z, u_Z))$, with $x'$
   804			a uniformly random point of $\ell_X$ sampled independently of
   805			$u$, is distributed according to
   806			$D_{\mathrm{v},i} \times D_{\mathrm{v},j}$. (No assertion is made
   807			about the joint conditional law of the pair $(u_X, u_Z)$.)
   808			\item If $\ell$ is axis-parallel, then $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Z$ are
   809			axis-parallel.
   810		\end{enumerate}
   811		(Property~3 is not part of the numbered statement in the source; see
   812		Remark~\ref{rem:qld-sublines-property-three}.)
   813	\end{lemma}
   814	\begin{proof}
   815		\uses{def:line-representative, def:ld-question-distribution,
   816			def:line-point-dist, def:ith-restricted-line, def:line,
   817			prop:line-equiv}
   818		The distribution $D$ is described by a sampling procedure. First sample
   819		$(\ell, u)$ from the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and write
   820		$u = (u_X, u_Z, \alpha, \beta)$, so that Property~1 holds by
   821		construction; all auxiliary randomness introduced below is sampled
   822		independently of $(\ell, u)$. We write $\chi$ for the index function of
   823		Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} at dimension $m$, whose
   824		classes $\chi^{-1}(i)$ for $i \in \{1, \dots, m\}$ partition $\F_q$
   825		into sets of equal size $q/m$, and $\chi_{2m+2}$ for the index function
   826		at dimension $2m+2$. The function $\chi_{2m+2}$, and with it the
   827		line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$ from which $(\ell, u)$ is
   828		drawn, is defined only when $2m+2$ divides $q$
   829		(Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}); admissibility of
   830		$(q,m,d)$ supplies only that $m$ divides $q$, and for admissible
   831		parameters with $m \ge 2$ the required divisibility fails, so this
   832		first step is an unresolved obligation of the source argument, recorded
   833		in Remark~\ref{rem:qld-4-7-divisibility} and analyzed in
   834		\cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}; the construction below is
   835		carried out for the parameters for which the distribution is defined.
   836		By a
   837		\emph{fresh diagonal direction pair} we mean a pair $(s', w')$ with
   838		$s'$ uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $w' \in \F_q^m$ having coordinates
   839		$1, \dots, \chi(s')-1$ equal to $0$ and the remaining coordinates
   840		uniformly random; this is exactly the law of the coordinate--direction
   841		data of the diagonal component of the line-point distribution over
   842		$\F_q^m$ (Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist}).
   843	
   844		If $\ell$ is axis-parallel, $\ell = (v, e_j)$ with
   845		$v = (v_X, v_Z, \alpha_0, \beta_0)$ and $j \in \{1, \dots, 2m+2\}$, set
   846		$\ell_X = (v'_X, e_{i_X})$ and $\ell_Z = (v'_Z, e_{i_Z})$ where: for
   847		$1 \le j \le m$, $i_X = j$ and $i_Z$ is uniformly random in
   848		$\{1,\dots,m\}$; for $m+1 \le j \le 2m$, $i_X$ is uniformly random and
   849		$i_Z = j - m$; for $2m+1 \le j \le 2m+2$, both $i_X$ and $i_Z$ are
   850		uniformly random; and $v'_X, v'_Z$ are the canonical line
   851		representatives of $v_X, v_Z$ for the chosen directions
   852		(Definition~\ref{def:line-representative}), so that $v_X \in \ell_X$
   853		and $v_Z \in \ell_Z$.
   854	
   855		If $\ell$ is diagonal, $\ell = (v, s, w)$, then by the construction of
   856		the diagonal component of the line-point distribution
   857		(Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} instantiated at
   858		dimension $2m+2$) the direction $w = (w_X, w_Z, \gamma, \delta)$ has
   859		coordinates $1, \dots, j-1$ equal to $0$, where $j = \chi_{2m+2}(s)$,
   860		and its remaining coordinates are uniformly random. These remaining
   861		coordinates may also vanish, so $w$ need not have a nonzero coordinate
   862		at index $j$ and may be the zero vector, in which case $\ell$ is a
   863		singleton (Definition~\ref{def:line}).
   864		% The source proof describes w as "a direction vector whose first
   865		% nonzero coordinate is j = chi(s)"
   866		% (references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex, proof
   867		% of lem:qld-sublines); the distribution delivers only the weaker
   868		% property recorded here, which is the one the argument uses. The
   869		% source also leaves the laws of s_X and s_Z unspecified ("chosen such
   870		% that chi(s_X) = j"); the uniform choices below are needed for the
   871		% exact marginals claimed in Property 2.
   872		Sample $\ell_X = (v'_X, s_X, w'_X)$ and $\ell_Z = (v'_Z, s_Z, w'_Z)$
   873		where: for $1 \le j \le m$, $w'_X = w_X$ and $w'_Z = w_Z$, with $s_X$
   874		uniformly random in the class $\chi^{-1}(j)$ and $s_Z$ uniformly
   875		random in the class $\chi^{-1}(1)$; for $m+1 \le j \le 2m$, the pair
   876		$(s_X, w'_X)$ is a fresh diagonal direction pair and $w'_Z = w_Z$,
   877		with $s_Z$ uniformly random in the class $\chi^{-1}(j-m)$; for
   878		$2m+1 \le j \le 2m+2$, both $(s_X, w'_X)$ and $(s_Z, w'_Z)$ are fresh
   879		diagonal direction pairs, sampled independently; and $v'_X, v'_Z$ are
   880		the canonical representatives of $v_X, v_Z$ for the directions
   881		$w'_X, w'_Z$.
   882	
   883		Property~3 is immediate from the procedure: when $\ell$ is
   884		axis-parallel, both $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Z$ are constructed to be
   885		axis-parallel. The containments in Property~2 hold for every point
   886		$u^\dagger = (u^\dagger_X, u^\dagger_Z, \alpha^\dagger,
   887		\beta^\dagger)$ of $\ell$: the block $u^\dagger_X$ differs from $v_X$

   889		inherited from $\ell$ (namely $e_j$ for axis-parallel $\ell$ with
   890		$1 \le j \le m$, and $w_X$ for diagonal $\ell$ with $1 \le j \le m$),
   891		and equals $v_X$ in all other cases, since then the corresponding
   892		block of the direction of $\ell$ vanishes; in either case

   894		$u^\dagger_Z \in \ell_Z$.

   896		For the distributional part of Property~2, observe first that
   897		$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is a function of $\ell$ and of the auxiliary

   902		compute them. Under both components of the line-point distribution the

   907		on $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z)$, the sampled point $u$ is uniformly

   910		the procedure itself.
   911	
   912		Condition on the component of the line-point distribution
   913		(axis-parallel or diagonal) and on $j$; the mixture of Property~2 is
   914		over these choices together with the fresh index choices, and the
   915		blocks $u_X, u_Z$ of $u$ are independent and uniform on $\F_q^m$,

   918		random point $u_X$ together with the canonical axis-parallel line

   920		$(\ell_X, u_X) \sim D_{\mathrm{ALine},j}$, while, conditioned

   922		uniformly random point $u_Z$ together with the canonical line through

   924		$(\ell_Z, u_Z) \sim D_{\mathrm{ALine},i_Z}$; the two pairs are
   925		functions of the disjoint independent data $u_X$ and $(u_Z, i_Z)$,
   926		hence independent. In the diagonal case with $1 \le j \le m$, the
   927		triple $(u_X, w_X, s_X)$ has $u_X$ uniform, $w_X$ with coordinates
   928		$1, \dots, j-1$ equal to $0$ and the remaining coordinates uniform,
   929		and $s_X$ uniform in $\chi^{-1}(j)$, which is exactly the law
   930		generating $D_{\mathrm{DLine},j}$; hence
   931		$(\ell_X, u_X) \sim D_{\mathrm{DLine},j}$, and similarly
   932		$(\ell_Z, u_Z) \sim D_{\mathrm{DLine},1}$ since $w_Z$ is uniform and
   933		$s_Z$ is uniform in $\chi^{-1}(1)$; the two pairs are functions of the
   934		disjoint independent data $(u_X, w_X, s_X)$ and $(u_Z, w_Z, s_Z)$,
   935		hence independent. The remaining cases are analogous: each of
   936		$(\ell_X, u_X)$ and $(\ell_Z, u_Z)$ is either built from the inherited
   937		direction block as above, or from a fresh axis index or fresh diagonal
   938		direction pair, in which case it is distributed as the uniform mixture
   939		over $i$ of $D_{\mathrm{v},i}$ for the corresponding type
   940		$\mathrm{v}$; and the two pairs are always functions of disjoint
   941		independent collections of the variables $u_X$, $u_Z$, the direction
   942		blocks, and the fresh auxiliary choices, hence independent conditioned
   943		on the component. Within each component this yields exactly the
   944		description of Property~2: the pair $(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is
   945		product-distributed according to the line marginals of
   946		$D_{\mathrm{v},i}$ and $D_{\mathrm{v},j}$, and, conditioned on
   947		$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$, each of $u_X$ and $u_Z$ is uniformly distributed
   948		on its line, because under each restricted distribution the point is
   949		uniform on the line conditionally on the line. The equivalent product
   950		formulations follow from the same conditional uniformity.
   951	\end{proof}

- [ ] F1 (blocker) `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:252` — The distance node’s `\leanok` is invalid because its global binary-observable and density hypotheses do not match three unconditional Lean declarations.
- [ ] F2 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/BooleanFourier.lean:45` — Eleven new public Boolean-character and Parseval declarations have no exact blueprint tags.
- [ ] F3 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/BLR.lean:63` — The new public BLR and Fourier-square results have no blueprint support entry or status tags.
- [ ] F4 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/NaimarkRounding.lean:69` — The new public Naimark-rounding construction and exact-linearity results have no blueprint support entry or status tags.
- [ ] F5 (changes) `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:219` — The Fourier support node omits the statement dependency `\uses{def:povm-conventions}` required by its binary-observable conclusion.
- [ ] F6 (changes) `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:196` — The normalization remark drops both averaging and squaring when describing the theorem’s distance bound.
- [ ] F7 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/BLR.lean:41` — Four docstring occurrences use the discouraged term “raw” as mathematical terminology for the operator distance.
- [ ] F8 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/BLR.lean:13` — “Consumes” and “consumed” describe mathematical dependencies using software-oriented language.
- [ ] F9 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/NaimarkRounding.lean:86` — The prose calls a projector family summing only to at most the identity a projective measurement rather than a projective submeasurement.
- [ ] F10 (changes) `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:209` — “Realigning the statement … is a separate task” is progress-report prose rather than mathematical exposition.

## Review

F1 is the most serious issue. The hypotheses at [ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:252](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-127-naimark-linearity-rounding/blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:252) govern the whole node. In Lean, however, `binaryObservableEffect` and `binaryObservableDistSq` accept arbitrary operators at [BooleanFourier.lean:307](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-127-naimark-linearity-rounding/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/BooleanFourier.lean:307) and [BooleanFourier.lean:316](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-127-naimark-linearity-rounding/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/BooleanFourier.lean:316), and the normalization identity at [BooleanFourier.lean:331](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-127-naimark-linearity-rounding/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/BooleanFourier.lean:331) requires neither binary observables nor a density operator. Only the two correlation identities impose those hypotheses. Split the universal definitions and normalization identity from the conditional correlation identities, or state their quantifiers separately.

F2-F4 are status-coverage gaps. The existing Fourier node omits the public character laws and `sum_operatorFourier_sq`. No public declaration from `BLR.lean` or `NaimarkRounding.lean` is represented. Add exact subordinate formalization-support nodes for these results, with their appropriate statement/proof status and dependencies. These additions must remain separate from `thm:linearity`; they do not justify adding `\leanok` to that source-labelled theorem.

For F5, the Fourier node’s conclusion explicitly assumes binary observables, whose mathematical definition is `def:povm-conventions`. Add that label to the node’s statement-level `\uses`.

For F6, replace the opening by “bounds the average squared state-dependent operator distance by \(\delta\).” Likewise, the next sentence must say that the **squared** binary-measurement distance is half the squared operator distance, and “the operator bound” should be “the average squared operator-distance bound.”

For F7, replace “raw distance” with “state-dependent operator distance” at lines 41 and 74, and “raw normalization” or “raw-distance normalization” with “operator-distance normalization” at lines 144 and 179.

For F8, replace “the Naimark dilation consumes” with “used in the Naimark dilation,” “in the form consumed after” with “after applying,” and the occurrence at [NaimarkRounding.lean:36](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-127-naimark-linearity-rounding/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/NaimarkRounding.lean:36) with “used to prove the averaged distance bound.”

For F9, `fourierNaimarkData` records projectors whose sum is only bounded above by the identity. Call this a “projective submeasurement”; `roundedFourierPVM` is the subsequent projective measurement resolving the identity.

For F10, drop the final process-oriented clause. The preceding sentences already state the mathematical discrepancy and its corrected normalization.

The `\notready` marker on `thm:linearity` remains appropriate: the Lean theorem still has an open proof, and its current \(\delta\) operator-distance conclusion is the documented false normalization. The other `\notready` markers in the chapter remain supported by open proofs or known statement discrepancies. Apart from F1’s statement mismatch, the two newly added proof-level `\leanok` claims have no direct proof holes.

Summary: 1 blueprint-Lean equivalence mismatch, 3 missing blueprint/status groups, 1 missing dependency, 1 mathematical-description error, and 4 prose issues.

VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED
